sentences.text: The genus Notochampsa is defined by its type species, Notochampsa istedana, which serves as the primary reference for the group.
Robert Broom first named this animal in 1904 after finding fossils in the lower Clarens Formation of the Karoo Supergroup in South Africa.
A second species, Notochampsa longipes, was later moved to its own genus, Erythrochampsa, in 1924.

Sidney Haughton created the family Notochampsidae to include Notochampsa, though the genus was historically used to include other protosuchian genera such as Dyoplax, Pedeticosaurus, Platyognathus, and Protosuchus.

Notochampsa was once assigned to the suborder Sphenosuchia, but a 2021 revision confirmed it as a valid taxon, placing it as the sister group to Orthosuchus within the monophyletic family Notochampsidae.
This creature lived between 201.4 and 184.2 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic.
